label: CDLI P000005 Uruk IV lexical tablet metadata
summary: CDLI catalogs P000005 (museum number VAT 15153) as a clay lexical tablet from Uruk (modern Warka), assigned to Uruk IV (ca. 3350–3200 BC), held in the Vorderasiatisches Museum, Berlin, with language undetermined.

label: CDLI P000005 column-one lexical signs and witness classification
summary: CDLI transcribes P000005 obverse column 1 as 1(N01) with ESZDA#, KAB, and DI@t?, marks the remainder broken, and lists the tablet as a witness to the Archaic Lu2 A composite P464118.

label: Distinct Ur III and Old Babylonian literary catalogue entries in ETCSL
summary: ETCSL separately lists an Ur III catalogue from Nibru (N1), an Old Babylonian catalogue from Nibru (N2), and an Old Babylonian catalogue possibly from Zimbir (B1); these listings do not themselves establish a transmission path among the catalogues.

sources.title: The Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature: Catalogue of all available compositions and translations

label: ETCSL listings for Gilgameš and Ḫuwawa Versions A and B
summary: ETCSL catalogs Gilgameš and Ḫuwawa as separate Version A (1.8.1.5) and Version B (1.8.1.5.1) entries, each offering transliteration and translation; those entries alone establish no copying direction or relative date.

sources.title: The Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature: Catalogue of all available compositions and translations

label: SAA 01 001 royal letter cataloguing and date limits
summary: SAAo catalogs SAA 01 001 (CDLI P224485; primary publication NL 039) as a Neo-Assyrian clay administrative letter from the Northwest Palace archive at Nimrud, attributed to Sargon II’s reign (721–705 BC) but explicitly undated, with sender the king and addressee Aššur-šarru-u[ṣur].

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

label: Reported Midas messenger and alliance claim in SAA 01 001
summary: In SAA 01 001 the royal writer quotes an earlier report that a messenger [of] Midas brought 14 men of Que previously sent by Urik to Urarṭu and declares that the Phrygian became an ally; these are reported statements in the letter, not independent verification of either event.

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

label: SAA 01 001 instruction to maintain Phrygian messenger contact
summary: SAA 01 001 directs its recipient not to withdraw a messenger from the Phrygian, to write amicably, and to monitor news about him; the instruction does not establish that the recipient complied.

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

label: Threatened two-sided pressure against Tabal in SAA 01 001
summary: In SAA 01 001 the royal writer proposes that the recipient pressure the kings of Tabal from one side while the Phrygian does so from the other; the source includes an ellipsis and does not confirm that the plan occurred.

sources.title: SAA 01 001. Midas Of Phrygia Seeks Detente (NL 039)

label: Sennacherib 015 claims confinement of Hezekiah in Jerusalem
summary: In RINAP Sennacherib 015, the first-person royal narrator claims to have confined Hezekiah in Jerusalem like a bird in a cage; this records an inscriptional claim rather than independent proof of the campaign outcome.

sources.title: Royal Inscriptions of the Neo-Assyrian Period: Sennacherib 015

label: Sennacherib 015 claims diversion of the Tebilti River
summary: In column vi of RINAP Sennacherib 015, the royal narrator reports changing the Tebilti River’s course, repairing erosion damage, and directing its outflow, with several portions of the translation editorially restored.

sources.title: Royal Inscriptions of the Neo-Assyrian Period: Sennacherib 015

label: Sennacherib 015 reports Nineveh orchard plots and a canal route
summary: In column viii of RINAP Sennacherib 015, the royal narrator reports dividing upstream meadowland into plots of two pānu for Nineveh’s citizens and cutting a canal from near Kisiri toward Nineveh’s plain; parts of the canal construction and route appear in brackets as editorial restorations.

sources.title: Royal Inscriptions of the Neo-Assyrian Period: Sennacherib 015
